newsitem.title: MOROCCO: French foreign minister starts Moroccan visit.
newsitem.headline: French foreign minister starts Moroccan visit.

text.p: France's Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine started on Monday a two-day visit to Morocco aiming to bring the North African country closer to the European Union, the official news agency MAP said.
Vedrine's visit was his first to a country outside the EU since the socialist government took power last month.
Earlier, Vedrine told MAP that he would raise visa procedures and ways to get the North African country closer to the European Union.

"French authorities have already taken concrete measures to ease visa procedures for Moroccans... Morocco and France could work together to identify snags hampering cooperation with the European Union and try to find solutions," he said.
Vedrine said the European Union and Mediterranean countries joined in the Barcelona accord had problems in the mechanics of financing their cooperation.
"We are aware of the finance difficulties affecting cooperation between the European Union and its southern partners," he said.
Vedrine is expected to meet King Hassan and Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali during his visit to Morocco.
Diplomatic sources said earlier that he was also expected to prepare for a visit to Morocco by French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin before the end of the year.
